note: Claims conservation science measured what sfumato/impasto/pointillism definitions leave out, down to paint-glaze layer width. Target article's own text: 'individual glaze layers only 1 to 2 micrometers thick... stacked as many as 30 times' from the 2010 X-ray fluorescence study, plus separate rheology and reading-list findings for impasto and pointillism.

Claims Romanesque painting has 'a rescue story of its own, a museum beating a dealer by hiring his crew.' Matches target article's own title verbatim: 'Romanesque Painting: A Museum Beat a Dealer by Hiring His Crew', and its body: the Catalan Museums Board 'hired Steffanoni's own crew for three more years' after losing the Santa Maria de Mur sale to dealer Ignasi Pollack.

Claims the checklist for painting's formal structure dates to a specific 1968 textbook, not older tradition. Fixed a pre-existing factual error in the source article during this verification pass: it previously said '1899 classroom textbook', but the target article (elements-of-art) documents the 7-item checklist (line/shape/form/space/value/color/texture) specifically to Otto Ocvirk's 'Art Fundamentals', earliest Internet Archive copy a 1968 printing -- Dow's 1899 book only had 3 elements (line/notan/color), not the 7-item list referenced here. Corrected cloisonne's body text from 1899 to 1968 to match; also independently cross-confirmed by mandala-art's own text referencing 'that piece found a system many people assume is ancient turning out to date only to a 1968 textbook'.

Claims the word mandala is documented nearly two thousand years before the earliest surviving pictorial mandala. Target article's own text: 'closer to two thousand years after that first documented use than to one' and FAQ states 'runs nearer 2,000 years than 1,000' between the Rig Veda's c. 1500-1200 BCE textual use and the 8th-9th century CE Tibetan pictorial sketches.
